findings.title: Four ApiService client methods have zero call sites in the Angular app
findings.description: `deleteProducerDetails`, `getAppliedTicketsByContract`, `getUnappliedTicketsByCustomer`, and `geocodeSearch` in api.service.ts are defined but never invoked anywhere else under client/src (verified by grepping every call site of every public method on ApiService). Two of these are confirmed, not just suspected, dead: (1) the corresponding backend endpoint's own code comment in ProducerDetailsService.cs:197-198 states outright that "deleteProducerDetails in api.service.ts is dead code" and the DELETE route is kept only as a defense-in-depth speed bump; (2) `geocodeSearch` wraps a single-address `/geocode/search` call that has been superseded by the batch `/geocode/batch` endpoint called directly via HttpClient from customer-map.component.ts — the wrapper was never removed after that migration. `getAppliedTicketsByContract` carries a doc comment on the neighboring method (line ~410) claiming applied tickets are "loaded lazily per-contract via {@link getAppliedTicketsByContract}", but no component actually calls it, so the documented lazy-load flow was never wired up. `getElevators` and `getBidMonths` in the same file are also currently uncalled but sit in the actively-developed bid-sheet feature area (recent WIP commits), so they are more plausibly near-term scaffolding than slop — deferred, not flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete deleteProducerDetails, getAppliedTicketsByContract, getUnappliedTicketsByCustomer, and geocodeSearch from api.service.ts (and the now-pointless doc-comment cross-reference at line ~410), or wire up the lazy per-contract ticket load the comment describes if that feature is still intended.
findings.resolution_notes: Deleted getUnappliedTicketsByCustomer, getAppliedTicketsByContract, deleteProducerDetails and geocodeSearch from api.service.ts, plus the doc cross-reference and the now-empty Geocoding section header. All four had zero call sites. One spec (ctrm-failure-visibility.spec.ts) used getUnappliedTicketsByCustomer as a text boundary marker when scanning the service source; it now uses the Planting Intention Operations section header, which covers the same contract-and-ticket section. The server endpoints behind them are untouched.

findings.title: SecurityAuditMiddleware never runs for the 401/403 cases it exists to log
findings.description: The middleware is placed after app.UseAuthorization() assuming the response status is finalized there, but ASP.NET Core's authorization middleware short-circuits (Challenge/Forbid) without calling next() on standard [Authorize] failures, which is virtually every endpoint. No IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler is registered to preserve pipeline continuation, so the security-guide's "log auth denials" control is silently dead code for most real 401/403s.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement a custom IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler (or hook the JWT OnForbidden/OnChallenge events) to log denials, rather than relying on downstream middleware the framework bypasses.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: DiagnosticsController bypasses the service layer and repeats the outbound-call anti-pattern the style guide singles out
findings.description: Injects three DbContexts and IHttpClientFactory directly, runs raw SQL via SqlQueryRaw, hand-writes upsert/seed logic with manual SaveChangesAsync, and loops over collections making one outbound HTTP call per item inside local try/catch instead of the GlobalExceptionHandler.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract schema-introspection, sync, and geocoding concerns into dedicated services (mirroring the existing CustomerSyncService pattern) and let exceptions flow to GlobalExceptionHandler.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Partially addressed — the duplicated Nominatim geocoding is de-duplicated and moved onto the resilient named client. The wider service-layer extraction is outstanding; severity re-rated to medium (AdminOnly policy, schema endpoints are Dev/QA-only). [2026-09-28] Re-checked: DiagnosticsController.cs (1105 lines) still injects OriginationDbContext/ApplicationDbContext/TradeUnitPreferencesDbContext/IHttpClientFactory directly and still runs SqlQueryRaw for schema introspection. Still open. [2026-10-13] Re-checked after the CTRM GraphQL-default and bin-sites/grain-on-farm releases: still 1105 lines, still injects the three DbContexts plus IHttpClientFactory directly, still raw SqlQueryRaw. The dead-CancellationToken-param issue in StartElevatorGeocode on this same file was fixed separately (see dotnet.dead-cancellation-token-param). Still open.
findings.resolution_notes: Behaviour-preserving extraction on fix_AuditCleanup_2026-10-13. DiagnosticsController (1105 -> 358 lines) now injects only IWebHostEnvironment, CustomerSyncService and six new interfaces under Services/Diagnostics/: ISchemaDiagnosticsService (connections, tables, tableschema, schema), ICtrmDiagnosticsService (ctrm, ctrm/contracts, ctrm/alias-batch, ctrm/producer-timing), ICommoditySeedService (commodities/seed), IElevatorCacheDiagnosticsService (elevator-cache/refresh, geocode, geocode-status, geocode-zip), IUsageRollupBackfillService (usage-rollups/backfill), IAppAccessDiagnosticsService (app-access-group-members). Method bodies moved verbatim; the DenyIfNotDevelopment/DenyIfProduction gates, [Authorize(Policy=AdminOnly)], every route string, the 400/409/202 mappings and the anonymous response shapes (now typed records with identical property names) stay in or match the controller. The per-item swallow-and-count in the two geocoding loops is kept on purpose (documented: one bad address must not abort a 1 req/sec walk); everything else still flows to GlobalExceptionHandler. The raw INFORMATION_SCHEMA reads remain SqlQueryRaw inside SchemaDiagnosticsService (no entity exists for catalog views; the table name is identifier-validated and passed as a SQL parameter). Registered by AddDiagnosticsServices() (Services/Diagnostics/DiagnosticsServiceCollectionExtensions.cs), one line in Program.cs. Pinned by DiagnosticsControllerRouteContractTests (all 16 verb+route pairs, response-type declarations, class attributes via reflection), DiagnosticsControllerGateTests (gate matrix per environment with strict mocks, 400/409/202), DiagnosticsServiceCollectionExtensionsTests (DI resolution incl. the controller), plus unit tests for the usage backfill, CTRM probes, app-access read and the Nominatim loop. DbContext-bound code (schema reads, commodity seed, elevator refresh, zip geocode, producer-timing customer lookup) is not unit-tested: no in-memory provider by project rule.

findings.title: Redundant re-fetch in ProducerDetailsRepository.UpsertAsync
findings.description: After rebuilding grain-on-farm and contact child rows in memory and saving, the method re-queries them via separate calls instead of reusing the in-memory values.

Applying the suggested fix would ship a bug. Reason documented in ProducerDetailsRepository.UpsertAsync.

findings.description: Only 20 of 49 components set ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; most of the shared UI kit and several feature components are entirely input()/signal-driven yet omit it.

findings.title: CustomerTradeUnit->Customer cascade delete breaks the codebase's own documented pattern, and manual rows now exist
findings.description: Every other FK to Customer in this file is explicitly NoAction with a comment explaining it's deliberate. CustomerTradeUnit's Customer FK is Cascade with no comment. The specific trigger (a hard DELETE of a Customer row) does not exist yet -- CustomerSyncService.SyncAsync is upsert + soft-delete only (IsActive = false), never a hard delete/rebuild -- so nothing destroys this data today. But the only thing preventing loss is that no code path currently issues a hard Customer delete, which is a fragile invariant to rely on for protecting manually-entered data.
findings.suggested_fix: Change CustomerTradeUnit's Customer FK to NoAction/Restrict to match the established pattern, independent of whether a hard-delete path is ever added. Also update docs/application-context/STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md, which still frames this as a future/pending decision ('Decide before that feature lands') -- the feature (feature_NewCustomerTradeUnits, merged 2026-05-27 per migration AddIsManualFlags) has already shipped.

Confirmed there is still no hard-delete/rebuild path for Customer (soft-delete only), so no data has actually been destroyed by this misconfiguration yet; the gap is the FK shape, not an observed incident.
[2026-10-13] Re-verified: ApplicationDbContext.cs:588-591 still configures CustomerTradeUnit's Customer FK as OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade), uncommented, while every sibling FK to Customer remains explicit NoAction with a rationale comment. findings.title: Unvalidated inbound X-Correlation-Id is trusted as the structured-log TraceId for every log line
findings.description: CorrelationIdMiddleware takes the inbound header with no length cap, character filter, or format check, then RequestContextMiddleware puts it into an ILogger.BeginScope TraceId field that every logger in the request inherits, plus it's echoed into log message templates in SecurityAuditMiddleware, GlobalExceptionHandler, and the OnAuthenticationFailed handler in Program.cs, and forwarded outbound via CorrelationIdOutboundHandler. An attacker-supplied value becomes the primary correlation key across the whole telemetry pipeline, enabling log-forging/injection into KQL-queried fields, correlation-dashboard pollution, cross-request correlation spoofing, and unbounded-length values inflating Log Analytics ingestion cost.
findings.suggested_fix: In CorrelationIdMiddleware, accept the inbound header only if it matches a safe format (e.g. GUID or bounded alphanumeric/hyphen, <=64 chars); otherwise discard it and mint a fresh ID, same as the no-header path.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-21] Re-verified: CorrelationIdMiddleware.IsWellFormed() now rejects anything over 64 chars or outside [A-Za-z0-9-_.:], falling back to Activity.TraceId or a fresh GUID. Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. Still resolved.

findings.title: Scheduled background services don't mint a per-run correlation id
findings.description: CustomerSyncBackgroundService, UsageAggregationBackgroundService, and UsageTrackingBackgroundService log via ILogger with good level discipline but never attach a per-execution id/scope, unlike HTTP requests which get TraceId via RequestContextMiddleware. If a nightly sync run misbehaves, there's no single field to filter Log Analytics down to just that run's log lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each ExecuteAsync run body in an ILogger.BeginScope(new { RunId = Guid.NewGuid() }) so all lines from one execution are filterable together.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-21] Re-verified and status corrected from resolved to open: CustomerSyncBackgroundService and UsageAggregationBackgroundService now wrap each run in _logger.BeginScope(...RunId...) (fixed via PR #615), but UsageTrackingBackgroundService — one of the three files this finding names — still has no per-run scope; its ExecuteAsync logs (start/stop/batch errors) carry no RunId. The fix was only 2/3 applied.

findings.title: Per-row template binding invokes an O(tickets x contracts) getter on every change-detection pass
findings.description: tickets-table.component.html calls spotTicketIds.has(ticket.id) inside a @for over group.tickets. spotTicketIds is a plain TS getter, not a computed(), that rebuilds a Set by iterating every ticket and, for each unapplied one, running contracts.some(...) over the full contracts array. Because it's called once per rendered ticket row and the component has no ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, this recomputes on every CD cycle triggered anywhere in the app, multiplying rendered-row-count x ticket-count x contract-count work repeatedly. For a producer with hundreds of tickets and dozens of contracts, this is a real, likely user-visible jank source on the Tickets tab.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert spotTicketIds (and the sibling unappliedTickets getter) to computed() signals, and add changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the component.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: tickets-table.component.ts:132 now declares `spotTicketIds = computed<Set<number>>(...)` with an inline comment naming this exact finding, so it recomputes only when tickets()/contracts() signals change rather than on every CD pass. OnPush itself is still not applied to this component, but that gap is separately tracked under performance.angular-onpush-coverage-gap, and the quadratic-recompute defect this finding targeted is genuinely closed via memoization regardless of change-detection strategy.

findings.title: Primary contracts table has no OnPush and repeats uncached per-row lookups in template bindings
findings.description: contracts-table.component.ts declares no changeDetection (defaults to Default strategy), so it re-runs full change detection on every app-wide tick. Its template calls getAppliedTickets(contract) (a .filter() over the full tickets() input with no memoization) and getPricingInfo(contract) up to 3 times per row, plus getPricingLinesForContract(contract) 4-5 times per expanded row. This is the table rendered on every customer-profile Contracts tab view, one of the most frequently opened screens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; memoize getAppliedTickets/getPricingInfo results per contract (e.g. a computed() Map similar to the existing pricingLinesMap/_deliveryStatsCache pattern already used for getDeliveryStats).
findings.notes:
[2026-09-21] Confirmed; part of the deferred OnPush work. [2026-09-28] Re-verified against current contracts-table.component.ts: still no changeDetection declared, getAppliedTickets() is still an unmemoized filter+sort over the full tickets() input, getPricingInfo()/getPricingLinesForContract() still called repeatedly per row via pricingLinesMap() lookups. No regression, no fix; still open.
[2026-10-13] Re-verified: still no changeDetection declared, getAppliedTickets() still unmemoized. No regression, no fix.
findings.resolution_notes: Two changes, behaviour unchanged. (1) getAppliedTickets and getPricingInfo are now lookups into computed Maps built once per data change (contracts, tickets, pricing lines) instead of a filter over every ticket and a recomputation per call; the template asked for each up to four times per row on every render. The applied-ticket matching rule is preserved exactly, including the asymmetric fallback (a contract with a sourceContractId still collects tickets that have no CTRM number but match by id). (2) ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, after checking what the template reads: signals, inputs, and three expansion Sets. The Sets are mutated only from click handlers and the input-driven customer-change effect; both paths now also call markForCheck explicitly, so the component is correct for any caller rather than relying on who invoked the toggle. A 30-test behaviour spec was written FIRST against the old implementation and the refactor had to pass it unchanged; it caught the one gap (direct toggle calls under OnPush) which was fixed in the component, not the spec. Verified by mutation: dropping the isApplied gate from the index and removing the id fallback for numbered contracts each failed the spec.

findings.title: Function calls used directly in template bindings re-run expensive work on every change-detection pass
findings.description: Verified across customer-profile.component.html (getContacts() inside a @for, backed by a fresh array allocation + sort on every evaluation), contracts-table.component.html (getPricingLinesForContract(contract) called 4 times per expanded row, ticketDisplayNumber(ticket) per applied-ticket row), and dashboard.component.html (commodityChipClass(chip.colorKey) inside a @for over planting chips). None of these are memoized via computed()/pipes.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert the highest-traffic offenders (especially ones that sort/filter arrays) to computed() signals or pure pipes.

[2026-10-13] Re-verified: same three template files, still no computed()/pipe conversion. No regression, no fix.

findings.title: Roughly half of standalone components skip OnPush change detection, compounding into full-tree re-evaluation
findings.description: Of 47 component.ts files, only 20 declare ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; the rest (including activity-summary, producer-insights, edit-customer-dialog, planting-intentions-table, home.component.ts, and both customer-map variants) run Default strategy. activity-summary.component.ts and tickets-table.component.ts in particular do multiple filter/reduce/sort passes over customer/contract/ticket arrays in plain getters/methods rather than computed(). This is a systemic risk that compounds any signal update in AppStateService into full-tree re-evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt OnPush as the default for new/touched components; prioritize converting the customer-profile subtree (home -> contracts-table, tickets-table, activity-summary) since that's the highest-traffic screen.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of angular.inconsistent-onpush-adoption. [2026-09-28] Re-counted: 23 of 49 component.ts files now declare OnPush (up slightly from 20/47), but the ratio and the named offenders (activity-summary, tickets-table, edit-customer-dialog, planting-intentions-table, home) are unchanged. Still open.
[2026-10-13] Re-verified: OnPush coverage now 23/49 (net one new component added, no new adopters). Named offenders unchanged.
[2026-10-13] Partial, deliberate. Converted to OnPush, each with an existing behaviour spec and each checked for non-signal state the template reads: the whole shared kit (badge, button, card x6 parts, table x6 parts, dialog x6 parts, select, input, toast-container), the three calculators, contracts-table (separately), and activity-summary (its one plain field, summaryText, is written in an effect that now also marks the view). input and select are ControlValueAccessors, so writeValue and setDisabledState now call markForCheck: a programmatic form write is not a DOM event and would otherwise never reach the native control under OnPush. Left on Default ON PURPOSE: planting-intentions-table (14 plain fields read by the template, several set from subscription callbacks, so OnPush would stop those renders without a signal refactor first), edit-customer-dialog (its spec blanks the template, so a render regression would be invisible), tickets-table, producer-insights, customer-map, unshipped-bushels, contract-pacing-card, year-over-year-chart (no spec at all), and home (one of the untested god components). Rule applied throughout: no OnPush without a rendering spec, and no sweep.

findings.title: Every usage-dashboard widget endpoint independently re-resolves the same user-scope set
findings.description: UsageDashboardService.GetUserIdSetAsync (called once per public method: GetSummaryAsync, GetUsersAsync, GetDailyActiveAsync, GetFeatureSessionsAsync, GetWeeklyTrendAsync, GetActivityBreakdownAsync, GetUnderusedFeaturesAsync, GetQueryLibraryUsageAsync, GetQuerySearchGapsAsync) re-runs GetSnapshotUserIdsAsync/GetSubtreeUserIdsAsync and GetExcludedUserIdsAsync from scratch for the same (tradeUnitKey, managerId) pair. The usage-dashboard page fires roughly nine of these as separate parallel HTTP requests on load, so the same small reference tables (UserTradeUnitSnapshots, UsageDashboardExcludedUsers) are queried up to 9x per page view instead of once. AppAccessService.GetAccessSetAsync (the more expensive external call in the same chain) is already IMemoryCache-backed, so this is the one piece of that resolution chain still uncached.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the resolved user-id HashSet per (tradeUnitKey, managerId) with a short TTL (seconds, matching page-load burst timing) the same way AppAccessService caches its access set, or hoist scope resolution to a single call the controller layer shares across the page's widget requests.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-28] New finding opened during reconciliation pass while reviewing the UsageDashboard feature added since 2026-09-21. Each underlying query is on a small table (no join fan-out), so this is a minor, inferred optimization opportunity rather than a proven bottleneck — flagged low severity, not measured.
[2026-10-13] Re-verified: GetUserIdSetAsync still called independently from 10 call sites in UsageDashboardService.cs with no caching. No regression, no fix.
[2026-10-13] Closed as a false positive after checking the code, not the finding text. The two previous re-verifications that called it uncached were wrong; worth weighting future re-verifications of this finding accordingly.
findings.resolution_notes: False positive: the fix the finding asks for has existed since commit 7c8454ae (2026-08-04), before the first audit ran. UsageDashboardService.GetUserIdSetAsync caches the resolved user-id set in IMemoryCache for 60 seconds, keyed per manager plus a UsageUniverseCacheState generation that an excluded-user edit bumps, and the cached set already has the exclusions applied, so the snapshot, subtree and exclusion reads happen once per manager per minute, not once per widget. The finding's (tradeUnitKey, managerId) key is also stale: trade-unit scoping was removed from the dashboard by the usage-for-all change. UsageDashboardServiceTests already pins the behaviour (several widget calls share one universe; the snapshot and exclusion reads verified Times.Once). Verified by mutation on 2026-10-13: bypassing the cache lookup fails that test.

findings.title: N+1 query in bid-insert race-reconciliation retry path is broader than initially scoped
findings.description: BidSheetRepository.ReconcileDuplicateBidInsertsAsync loops over EVERY ChangeTracker entry in EntityState.Added for BidSheetLocationBid, not just the one that triggered the unique-constraint exception, issuing one FirstOrDefaultAsync per entity to check for a DB-side collision. Triggered from BulkUpsertBidsAsync's SaveChanges catch block, so a single unique-constraint race during a large bulk upsert (many locations x commodities x months) fans out to one round trip per pending insert, not just per actual collision.
findings.suggested_fix: Batch-load all potentially colliding rows in one query keyed by the tuple set, then reconcile in memory (mirroring BulkUpsertBidsAsync).
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: BidSheetRepository.cs:463-503 ReconcileDuplicateBidInsertsAsync now issues one batched query keyed by distinct LocationId/CropYear across all pending Added entities, then reconciles in-memory via a dictionary keyed on (LocationId, CommodityCode.ToUpperInvariant(), CropYear, Month) -- replacing the prior per-entity FirstOrDefaultAsync fan-out. Inline comments explicitly reference the N+1 pattern being avoided.

findings.title: ProducerDetails upsert deletes and reinserts all child rows instead of diffing

findings.title: qa-setup.sql can silently resurrect a trade-unit catalog schema that was deliberately removed
findings.description: scripts/qa-setup.sql contains IF NOT EXISTS CREATE TABLE blocks for TradeUnits, TradeUnitGroups, and GroupTradeUnits. Migration 20260513051734_RemoveTradeUnitCatalog.cs explicitly drops all three of these same tables, with a comment stating they were deliberately superseded by the TradeUnitPreferences DB view vw_UserTradeUnitAccess and direct ODS lookups -- a documented architectural decision, not an accident. Because qa-setup.sql's guard only checks whether the table exists, running this script today against any environment where RemoveTradeUnitCatalog has already applied would silently resurrect the deprecated catalog tables, undoing that architecture decision under the guise of an innocuous create-missing-tables script.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the TradeUnits/TradeUnitGroups/GroupTradeUnits blocks from qa-setup.sql (or delete the whole script, consistent with the other stale-script findings, since EF migrations are the actual source of truth for schema state).
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Re-verified: scripts/qa-setup.sql no longer exists in the repo at all -- deleted outright rather than just stripping the TradeUnits/TradeUnitGroups/GroupTradeUnits blocks, which also resolves the finding. Fixed via PR #615. Still resolved.

findings.title: _VerifySchema.sql's hand-maintained tracking lists have already drifted from each other, defeating its own purpose
findings.description: scripts/_VerifySchema.sql hand-maintains 4 parallel lists (@Tables, @Columns, @UniqueIndexes, @Migrations) that its own header comment says must all be updated after every new migration. @Migrations stops 19 entries in while the repo has ~30 more migrations since; @Columns was partially updated for 3 recent columns while @Tables was never updated for at least 5 tables created by migrations in between. findings.title: [ApiController] automatic model-validation responses never use the standard error envelope
findings.description: All 23 controllers carry [ApiController], and Program.cs never configures ApiBehaviorOptions.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory. So any data-annotation failure on the 21 validated request DTOs is short-circuited by the ASP.NET Core framework default into RFC7807 ValidationProblemDetails JSON before GlobalExceptionHandler or the app's own ValidationException ever run. This is the single most common validation-failure path across the whole write surface, and it never matches the mandated {error:{code,message,details,traceId,timestamp,instance}} shape, while the exact same conceptual failure thrown manually as ValidationException elsewhere produces a completely different shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure builder.Services.Configure<ApiBehaviorOptions>(o => o.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory = ctx => ...) to build the same ApiErrorResponse envelope GlobalExceptionHandler produces for a thrown ValidationException, sourcing error.details from ModelState.

findings.title: No client-side type models the backend's standard error contract, enabling systemic silent swallowing
findings.description: No ApiError class/interface exists anywhere in the Angular app corresponding to the backend's documented {error:{code,message,details,traceId,timestamp,instance}} envelope. ApiService.handleError() unwraps every HttpErrorResponse into a bare Error object with an unsafely-cast .status property bolted on, discarding error.code, error.details, and error.traceId outright. Because there is no shared, typed error surface for call sites to branch on, roughly two dozen .subscribe({error: () => {}}) blocks and DataPreloadService's uniform catchError(() => of([])) pattern (11 datasets) each independently improvise or skip error handling. This is the root CONTRACT gap; the angular-domain finding describes its component-level symptom.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce one typed ApiError class built centrally in ApiService.handleError() (code, message, details, traceId, category derived from HTTP status), make it the only error type ApiService ever throws, and require callers to branch on .category instead of improvising per call site.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; the contract-level root cause of angular.no-typed-error-contract-silent-swallowing. Note "discards error.details outright" is overstated — handleError does read details[].message; it discards code, traceId (now fixed) and the structured array. [2026-09-28] Re-verified against current api.service.ts handleError() (lines 88-124): still a bare Error with .status/.traceId bolted on, no ApiError type, error.code still never read. No regressions, no change since prior pass. [2026-10-13] Calibration re-run. Re-read handleError() on current HEAD (lines 88-124, after the 403/401 branches): unchanged — still builds a bare Error with .status/.traceId bolted on via unsafe casts, no ApiError type anywhere in client/src, error.code still never read. No regression, no fix.

findings.title: A handful of controllers return raw strings/anonymous objects instead of throwing through GlobalExceptionHandler
findings.description: UsageDashboardController, CustomersController, BidSheetController, and DiagnosticsController return ad hoc bodies directly instead of throwing ValidationException/BusinessException, unlike 59 call sites across 24 other files that correctly throw typed exceptions. The bare-string case is worst: ASP.NET serializes it as a raw JSON string body, and Angular's handleError() fallback chain cannot extract anything from a plain string, so it falls through to a generic error message instead of the intended user-facing text.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with throw new ValidationException(...) / throw new BusinessException(...) so they flow through GlobalExceptionHandler like the rest of the app.

findings.title: The only real producer of HTTP 429 never gets a Retry-After header or the standard envelope
findings.description: Program.cs's AddRateLimiter fixed-window limiter is the sole path in the codebase that returns 429. No OnRejected callback is configured, so the rejection is written directly by RateLimiterMiddleware with an empty body and no headers, entirely bypassing GlobalExceptionHandler. GlobalExceptionHandler's own code that sets Retry-After: 30 for statusCode 429 is therefore dead code for the one status it explicitly names, since exceptions never produce 429 in this app.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure options.OnRejected on AddRateLimiter to write the standard ApiErrorResponse envelope and set Retry-After before returning.

findings.title: Diagnostics elevator-geocoding bypasses the app's own nominatim retry/circuit-breaker pipeline

An older, uncancellable in-flight fetch can still land and overwrite the freshly-restored cached data because its captured request id still matches.

findings.title: DP-contracts fetch in build-list can reapply stale-trade-unit data after the shared cache was correctly reset
findings.description: DataPreloadService calls appState.clearDpContractsCache() reactively on trade-unit change. BuildListComponent._ensureDpForQuery() has no request-id or TU-match check on its response handler, only a guard against a second concurrent call. If the user switches trade units while a DP fetch for the old TU is in flight, the reset fires first, then the stale response lands and calls appState.setDpContracts(data), re-flipping dpContractsLoaded=true with the wrong trade unit's rows, silently corrupting a cache shared across the whole app.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the trade-unit key at fetch start and discard the response in _ensureDpForQuery's subscribe if appState.selectedTradeUnits() no longer matches it.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _ensureDpForQuery now captures fetchedForTu and checks an isStale() closure before writing the response into the shared cache.

findings.title: Ticket self-heal effect can adopt another trade unit's ticket data
findings.description: _appStateTicketsEffect compares appState.tickets().length > this.tickets().length with no check that the appState data actually belongs to the currently selected trade unit. appState.tickets is cleared by a separate singleton (DataPreloadService, via clearTicketsCache()) reacting independently to the same selectedTradeUnits signal this component's own _tuEffect/_loadFresh(true) reacts to. Angular gives no ordering guarantee between these two independent subscribers, so during a trade-unit switch there's a window where this component's local tickets is already [] (freshly cleared for the new TU) while appState.tickets still holds the previous TU's larger set -- the effect then copies the old TU's tickets into the new TU's context and marks _ticketsReady=true, letting a ticket-dependent query silently run against the wrong trade unit's deliveries.
findings.suggested_fix: Tag cached ticket data with the trade-unit key it was fetched for (or re-check appState.selectedTradeUnits() matches) before adopting it, instead of a bare length comparison.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _appStateTicketsEffect now compares appState.ticketsTradeUnitKey() against the currently selected TU and bails before adopting on a mismatch, with a comment naming this exact race.

The canonical isContractUnconfirmed(), documented as the same rule the Insights Unconfirmed Contracts category and this same file's refine-panel checkbox use, treats NULL/empty status as unconfirmed too. A contract that's never had a confirmation status set (the most common unconfirmed case) appears in Insights and the refine-panel checkbox but is silently dropped from producers-with-unconfirmed-contracts typed into Build A List.

findings.title: New bid-sheet location inserts aren't protected against the same unique-constraint race the rest of the class handles
findings.description: BidSheetRepository.BulkUpsertBidsAsync saves newly-discovered BidSheetLocation rows via a bare SaveChangesAsync with no try/catch, while CreateLocationAsync and UpdateLocationAsync both wrap their saves in a catch for unique violations and attempt reconciliation. If two concurrent bid-sheet submissions both need to create the same new location (same Name+TradeUnitCode, unique index), one throws an unhandled DbUpdateException and the entire bulk save fails (whole batch of bids lost) instead of reconciling like every other collision path in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the new-location SaveChangesAsync call in the same IsUniqueViolation catch/reconcile pattern used elsewhere in the class.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 verified] Premise CONFIRMED against the databases: PROD carries UQ_BidSheetLocations_Name_TradeUnit (unique), so the guard protects a real race there. Dev and QA do not — both run the feature_BidSheetRemodelAndBarchartFeed schema, where MakeBidSheetLocationsGlobal dropped per-TU name uniqueness. The index exists in PROD but in NO migration (hand-rolled migrate-bid-sheet.sql created it outside EF), so a duplicate location name fails in PROD and nowhere else. The comments in BidSheetRepository.cs naming this index are accurate — do not correct them. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: BulkUpsertBidsAsync's new-location save is now wrapped in catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (IsUniqueViolation(ex)), calling a dedicated ReconcileDuplicateLocationInsertsAsync.

findings.title: CreateLocationAsync/UpdateLocationAsync's reconcile-the-race catch block never actually reconciles anything

Since neither method adds any bid entities, the call always returns false and falls through to rethrow. The log message and comment are misleading: a genuine location-name race is never recovered, it just wastes a query before behaving exactly as if there were no catch block.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement real location-collision reconciliation (re-fetch by Name+TradeUnitCode and merge), or remove the misleading catch/log/comment since it currently does nothing.

findings.title: Dashboard upsert methods scope their existing-row lookup to item[0]'s TradeUnitKey/Year, not each item's own
findings.description: UpsertPlantingEstimatesAsync builds existingMap from estimates[0].TradeUnitKey/PlantingYear alone, then loops over every item in the batch against that single map (mirrored for market-shares/actual-harvest). Nothing enforces that every item shares item 0's TU/Year. A batch containing an item for a different TU/Year that already has a DB row gets mis-scoped as not-found, attempts an INSERT, and throws on the unique index, aborting the whole transaction including unrelated correctly-scoped items.
findings.suggested_fix: Key existingMap off the full (TradeUnitKey, PlantingYear, Crop) tuple across all distinct combinations present in the request, not a single scope assumed from item 0.

findings.title: Usage tracking silently drops every request that ends in an unhandled exception
findings.description: UsageTrackingMiddleware is registered after UseExceptionHandler in the pipeline, so it's nested inside the exception handler's scope. Its InvokeAsync calls await _next(context) then builds/writes the UserActivityRecord afterward -- if the downstream call throws, that code never runs, so the request is invisible to usage analytics. Same root cause as the already-logged SecurityAuditMiddleware finding: pipeline position assumes a normal return that the framework short-circuits on exceptions, undercounting real error-rate/session data specifically for the failures that matter most.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the downstream call in try/finally so the activity record (with the real or a synthesized 5xx status code) is always recorded regardless of exception.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: InvokeAsync now wraps await _next(context) in try/finally, with a comment noting the record is written even on an unhandled exception.

findings.title: GeocodeService.SearchAsync caches only the first result but returns the full list, so a later cache hit silently truncates to 1
findings.description: A cache miss calls Nominatim, builds up to limit results (up to 5), returns the full list, but caches only results[0]. The cache-hit branch then returns a list containing exactly that one cached point. The same query+limit returns a different-shaped result depending purely on cache warmth -- a disambiguation dropdown that showed 5 candidates on first search silently shows 1 on the next identical search.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the full result list keyed by query+limit, or skip caching multi-result searches entirely.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: SearchAsync now does _cache.Set(cacheKey, results, ...) with the full list, and the cache-hit branch returns a defensive copy of that full list rather than a single point.

findings.title: GeocodeBatchAsync doesn't use the shared rate-limiting semaphore, allowing bursts past Nominatim's 1 req/sec policy
findings.description: GeocodeService is registered as a singleton specifically so _rateLimiter (SemaphoreSlim) and _lastNominatimCall serialize all Nominatim calls across concurrent requests; GeocodeSingleAsync and SearchAsync both acquire the semaphore first. GeocodeBatchAsync never touches either, only self-pacing with its own internal 1100ms delay between items in its own loop. Two concurrent callers will send simultaneous requests to Nominatim, violating the documented 1 req/sec limit and risking an IP-level throttle that would break geocoding app-wide.
findings.suggested_fix: Have GeocodeBatchAsync acquire _rateLimiter and honor _lastNominatimCall the same way GeocodeSingleAsync does.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: GeocodeBatchAsync now calls await _rateLimiter.WaitAsync(...) per item, with a comment explaining why it acquires per-item rather than for the whole batch.

findings.title: In-flight HTTP request dedup cache can be evicted while the underlying call is still pending
findings.description: ApiService._dedupe() builds request.pipe(shareReplay({bufferSize:1, refCount:false}), finalize(() => this._inFlight.delete(key))). Because finalize sits downstream of shareReplay, its teardown runs per individual subscriber's own unsubscribe, not once when the shared underlying HTTP call itself completes. DataPreloadService subscribes to these calls inside a switchMap keyed on trade-unit selection; switching trade units unsubscribes from the old TU's in-flight request, which immediately deletes its _inFlight cache entry even though refCount:false keeps the real HTTP call alive in the background. Switching back to that TU before the original response lands fires a brand-new duplicate HTTP request against the same endpoint the cache exists to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Move finalize upstream of shareReplay (request.pipe(finalize(...), shareReplay(...))) so cleanup ties to the shared source's completion, not each subscriber's teardown.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _dedupe() now pipes finalize(...) upstream of shareReplay(...), with a comment explaining exactly why the ordering matters for switchMap-driven unsubscription.

findings.title: Contract pacing is computed two different, contradictory ways in the same service
findings.description: The free-text pacing/negative-pacing NLQ handler in applyContractFilters computes this-year/last-year booked bushels from getOpenContracts(c) (excludes any contract with a closedDate). The refine-panel Down harvest pace flag in applyRefinementFilters computes the identical metric from ALL contracts regardless of closedDate. A producer who closed out a large contract this year shows as down pacing (or a different number) depending on whether the user types a pacing query versus checking the refine-panel box on the same saved list -- same business question, two different answers from the same file.

findings.title: Manage-Members customer search has no in-flight request cancellation
findings.description: searchMembers() debounces via setTimeout/clearTimeout, but once a debounced call actually fires the API request, a subsequent keystroke only clears the next timer -- it doesn't cancel the already-in-flight searchCustomers call. Two overlapping requests (e.g. for 'abc' then 'abcd') can resolve out of order, and whichever resolves last overwrites memberSearchResults, so the UI can show results for a stale, already-abandoned search term.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the debounced search through an RxJS Subject + switchMap (or track a request id and ignore stale responses) instead of a raw setTimeout+subscribe.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. findings.title: A refine change can be permanently stranded if it lands while a different note-scope fetch is in flight
findings.description: _ensureNotesForQuery is a no-op whenever _scopedNotesFetchInFlight is already true, silently dropping the request for the new scope. _commitRefinements calls it exactly once when staging a refine; if that call is swallowed because an older scoped fetch (different keyword/pinned/author/window combo) is still in flight, the older fetch's next handler stores the old scope's key, _criteriaReadiness for the newly staged refine never becomes true, and nothing else re-invokes _ensureNotesForQuery for the new scope. The staged refine (and its loading spinner/disabled Apply) can be stuck until the user makes another refine change.
findings.suggested_fix: When a scoped-notes fetch resolves, re-check the current desired scope (not just the one captured at fetch start) and re-fire _ensureNotesForQuery if it has since changed.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: a _supersededNoteScopeRequest slot plus _retryScopedNotesIfSuperseded() now re-fires _ensureNotesForQuery with the swallowed scope once the in-flight fetch resolves, on both the next and error paths.

findings.title: Ticket dates compared with local-time getters can misclassify Jan 1 tickets
findings.description: Ticket.date is a bare yyyy-MM-dd string, which the JS Date constructor parses as UTC midnight. hasDeliveriesThisYear then reads d.getFullYear(), a local-time getter, so for any user in a negative-UTC-offset zone (all US time zones), a ticket dated Jan 1 renders as Dec 31 of the prior year, wrongly excluding that delivery from has-deliveries-this-year. The file already has a purpose-built UTC-safe parser (parseNoteTime) for exactly this class of bug on notes, but ticket dates aren't run through an equivalent helper.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse t.date with UTC-aware getters (getUTCFullYear()) or split the yyyy-MM-dd string directly instead of running it through local-time Date getters.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: hasDeliveriesThisYear now reads d.getUTCFullYear() with a comment explaining the prior local-time year-boundary bug.

findings.title: DiagnosticsController hand-rolls Nominatim geocoding twice instead of using the existing rate-limited/cached IGeocodeService

The in-code comment on the cache-hit path already stated the intent ("handing back the cached instance would let any caller mutation corrupt the entry for everyone"); the miss path simply did not follow it.

findings.title: Component subscribe() calls with no takeUntilDestroyed/DestroyRef cleanup
findings.description: EditCustomerDialogComponent makes 7 apiService.subscribe() calls (loading planting commodities, trade units, customer trade units, planting intentions, commodities, customers, and removing a dormant trade unit) with no DestroyRef, no takeUntilDestroyed(), and no ngOnDestroy anywhere in the 1045-line file. Both are non-singleton components that are mounted and torn down repeatedly (a dialog opened per customer, a table rendered per customer detail view), so an in-flight request that outlives the component can still call .set()/mutate component state after destruction, and repeated opens can pile up concurrent in-flight subscriptions. This is the style guide's 'Use takeUntilDestroyed() for observable cleanup' rule (Component Best Practices #3).

[2026-10-13] Re-checked: edit-customer-dialog.component.ts still has 8 subscribe() calls (grew from 7) with no DestroyRef/takeUntilDestroyed anywhere in the file; planting-intentions-table.component.ts still injects DestroyRef (line 46) but none of its 3 subscribe() calls pipe through it. No change. Still open.

findings.title: CTRM dependency-call duration is computed but never reaches structured logs, only a non-prod response header
findings.description: CtrmProvenance.RecordContracts/RecordTickets stamp ContractsMs/TicketsMs (elapsed time for each CTRM contracts/tickets read) via a Stopwatch, but the only consumers are CtrmProvenanceMiddleware (which emits them as a Server-Timing header, and only when !environment.IsProduction, so this never reaches prod) and DiagnosticsController (an on-demand manual endpoint). No repository or client code passes these values to ILogger, so durationMs never appears on the many LogInformation/LogWarning/LogError lines already emitted for CTRM reads in CtrmContractRepository.cs, CtrmTicketRepository.cs, and CtrmGraphQlClient.cs. The style guide lists durationMs as a required-when-applicable field for dependency calls (4.1) and calls out dependency calls that materially degrade latency as a required log point (7.2). This integration has known, explicitly-documented severe latency (a cold contracts(customerIds:) page for 500 producers is 22-25s per CtrmServerTimeoutRetry.cs comments, right at the 30s HC0045 timeout), so a call that is slow-but-succeeds today is invisible in Log Analytics/App Insights in production; only an outright failure is diagnosable from logs, and a support engineer investigating a slow-but-successful CTRM page load in prod has to reproduce the issue rather than query for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass provenance.ContractsMs/TicketsMs (or a locally-scoped Stopwatch around the CTRM read) into the existing success/failure log lines in CtrmContractRepository and CtrmTicketRepository as a structured {DurationMs} property, so slow-but-successful CTRM reads are queryable in Log Analytics without needing the dev-only Server-Timing header or the manual diagnostics endpoint.
findings.notes: [2026-09-28] Found during logging reconciliation while reviewing the CTRM GraphQL integration merged since the 2026-09-21 pass (feature_CtrmGraphQlSpike). Confirmed via grep: ContractsMs/TicketsMs are set in CtrmProvenance.cs and read only in CtrmProvenanceMiddleware.cs (header, non-prod) and DiagnosticsController.cs (manual endpoint) — no _logger call in the Ctrm/ directory references either property.
findings.resolution_notes: The per-producer contract and ticket reads now carry {DurationMs} on both their success and their failure log line, taken from the ContractsMs/TicketsMs the provenance object already measured. On the failure paths the provenance Record call was moved above the log so the number is populated: how long CTRM took to FAIL is the more useful of the two, since it separates a fast rejection from a gateway timeout. DurationMs is appended rather than woven into the message text on purpose, so the CTRM contracts: N for producer X prefix the turn-on runbook and the App Service log stream look for stays intact. This matters more than its medium severity suggests once PROD flips to CTRM: the API carries no Application Insights SDK, the diagnostics endpoints are blocked in Production, and the Server-Timing header carrying the same numbers is emitted outside Production only, so these log lines are the only queryable record of CTRM latency in PROD.

findings.title: CtrmKeepWarmService warm cycles do not scope their logs with a per-cycle correlation id
findings.description: CtrmKeepWarmService.WarmActiveSetsAsync runs every Ctrm:KeepWarmMinutes (default 5) and, per active producer set, issues a contracts read, a ticket-history read, and a Spot Loads read, logging a warning per read that does not complete plus a final LogInformation summarizing sets maintained and elapsed seconds. None of these lines carry a per-cycle or per-set identifier the way HTTP requests get TraceId via RequestContextMiddleware, so if two or more producer sets are warmed in the same cycle (or overlapping cycles under load) and one logs failures, Log Analytics has no field to filter down to just that set/cycle's lines the way section 6 (correlation) and the existing accepted finding logging.background-job-runs-lack-correlation-id already call out for other background services. Unlike UsageTrackingBackgroundService (accepted as exempt because it is a trivial 5-second flush loop), this service does substantive multi-step, multi-producer-set I/O each cycle, so a run/set-scoped id would answer a real question ('which cycle logged this failure and what else happened in it').
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each WarmActiveSetsAsync cycle (or each per-set iteration) in _logger.BeginScope(new { CycleId = Guid.NewGuid(), Producers = codes.Count }), matching the pattern already used in CustomerSyncBackgroundService and UsageAggregationBackgroundService.
findings.notes: [2026-09-28] Found during logging reconciliation while reviewing the CTRM GraphQL integration. Verified CtrmKeepWarmService.cs has no BeginScope call anywhere in the file, unlike the two background services already fixed for this pattern via PR #615.
findings.resolution_notes: WarmActiveSetsAsync now opens an ILogger scope per cycle carrying ServiceName, Operation (CtrmKeepWarm.Cycle), a fresh TraceId and the set count, matching the fields CustomerSyncBackgroundService and UsageAggregationBackgroundService already use and the fields RequestContextMiddleware puts on HTTP requests. Every warning and the closing summary in a cycle now share one filterable id. Done alongside the keep-warm test work since it is the same method; it was not in the batch originally picked.

findings.title: ReadInt/ReadBool config-parsing helpers independently reimplemented 6 times across the new CTRM vertical
findings.description: The CTRM GraphQL integration merged since the 2026-09-21 audit (Services/Ctrm, Infrastructure/Ctrm) reimplements the same private ReadInt(string key, int fallback) / ReadBool(string key, bool fallback) config-parsing helpers independently in six places: CtrmContractReader.cs, CtrmTicketReader.cs, CtrmTicketRepository.cs, CtrmServerTimeoutRetry.cs, CtrmTradeUnitThrottle.cs, and CtrmKeepWarmService.cs. Most copies are byte-identical (int.TryParse/bool.TryParse over _configuration[key]?.Trim()), but CtrmKeepWarmService.cs's copy drops the NumberStyles/CultureInfo.InvariantCulture arguments the others use, and CtrmTicketRepository.cs's ReadBool drops the fallback parameter entirely (different signature) — classic copy-paste drift where the duplicates have already started to diverge.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract one internal static CtrmConfig.ReadInt/ReadBool(IConfiguration, key, fallback) helper (CtrmServerTimeoutRetry.cs and CtrmTradeUnitThrottle.cs already use the static-with-IConfiguration-parameter shape) and have all six call sites delegate to it, fixing the CultureInfo/signature drift in the same pass.
findings.notes: Found while reviewing the new CTRM GraphQL integration (merged since the 2026-09-21 clean-slop pass) for the categories in the clean-slop skill (copy-paste drift). Confirmed via direct grep + read of all six files; StableHash(IEnumerable<string>) is also byte-identical between CtrmContractReader.cs and CtrmTicketReader.cs but was left out of the fix scope since it is only duplicated twice and is already noted as intentionally mirrored in the two Switch classes' doc comments.
findings.resolution_notes: Added CtrmConfig.ReadInt/ReadBool(IConfiguration, key, fallback) in Infrastructure/Ctrm. All six sites now delegate: CtrmContractReader, CtrmTicketReader and CtrmTicketRepository keep one-line private wrappers so their ~25 call sites are unchanged, while CtrmServerTimeoutRetry and CtrmTradeUnitThrottle call CtrmConfig directly since their signature already matched. A seventh inline copy in CtrmTicketRepository.RecentTicketDaysFrom was folded in too. Both drifts named in the finding are fixed: CtrmKeepWarmService now parses with InvariantCulture like everything else, and CtrmTicketRepository.ReadBool takes an explicit fallback instead of meaning false implicitly (its one call site now reads fallback: false). System.Globalization imports left unused by the change were removed from three files.

findings.title: ResolveScoularIdAsync duplicated near-verbatim between CtrmContractRepository and CtrmTicketRepository
findings.description: CtrmContractRepository.cs and CtrmTicketRepository.cs each define a private async Task<string?> ResolveScoularIdAsync(long customerId, string? scoularId, CancellationToken) that is identical apart from the log message ("CTRM contracts" vs "CTRM tickets") and one extra explanatory comment in the contract version. Both look up appContext.Customers by customerId and return the trimmed ScoularId, falling back with a warning log when the customer has none.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the lookup into a small shared helper (e.g. a method on a CtrmCustomerCodes-adjacent class, since that file already owns producer/customer code concerns) parameterized by the log prefix, or accept the duplication as two call sites is a low bar for extraction — flagging for awareness rather than urgency.
findings.notes: Found while reviewing the new CTRM GraphQL integration for copy-paste drift. Low severity: only two call sites, low churn risk, and the two Repository classes are already documented as deliberately parallel (see ContractRepositorySwitch/TicketRepositorySwitch doc comments).
findings.resolution_notes: Extracted CtrmProducerCode.ResolveAsync(appContext, logger, what, customerId, scoularId, ct). Both repositories now delegate through a one-line wrapper, passing their own logger so the warning keeps its own category and their own label so the message text is unchanged. Deliberately a new file rather than a method on CtrmCustomerCodes, which is pure and has no database dependency.

findings.title: contract-status.ts's harvest-pacing and confirmation-status rules are untested despite each existing to fix a documented drift bug
findings.description: computeHarvestPacePct's own doc comment says it exists because the free-text pacing query and the refine-panel checkbox used to compute year-over-year booked-bushel pacing differently and gave different answers to the same question -- it now contains non-obvious rules (pace against the producer's own max delivery year, not calendar year; include ALL contracts not just open ones; same-point-last-year cutoff) with zero test asserting any of them. isContractUnconfirmed and isContractCustomerConfirmed are also non-inverses by design (both return false for terminal Fulfilled/Cancelled contracts) -- an easy rule to flip back to a naive negation with no CI signal. None of the four exported functions in this file have a spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Add contract-status.spec.ts: pace-pct cases (no contracts, no prior-year data, mid-crop-year cutoff, straddling calendar year-end), and the Fulfilled/Cancelled non-inverse case for isContractUnconfirmed vs isContractCustomerConfirmed.
findings.notes: [2026-09-28] New since the last test-gaps reconciliation (2026-09-22) -- file's own comments describe a previously-shipped pacing-drift bug between two call sites, the same 'converter exists to fix a documented bug' pattern the date-timezone-json-converters finding covered on the .NET side.
findings.resolution_notes: Added contract-status.spec.ts (30 tests) covering all four exported functions. The headline case is pinned directly: for a terminal Fulfilled or Cancelled contract the customer never confirmed, BOTH isContractUnconfirmed and isContractCustomerConfirmed return false, with a companion test proving they ARE exact opposites for every non-terminal contract, which is what makes collapsing one into a negation of the other easy to miss in review. Also covers the overdue rules including the shared sub-0.1% completion threshold, and the pacing rules: max-delivery-year bucketing, the calendar-year straddle, all contracts counting rather than only open ones, and the same-point-last-year cutoff. Verified by mutation: collapsing the two predicates into a naive negation failed the non-inverse test. Fixtures are built from the real Contract type with no casts, so a model change breaks compilation.

findings.title: CtrmCustomerCodes.Normalize, the shared customerIds filter guard, has zero test coverage
findings.description: Normalize's own doc comment documents a measured production failure mode: an 8+ character customer code makes the whole customerIds-filtered CTRM call fail with a generic error, taking every producer in that chunk down with it, not just the offending one. NormalizeKeepingAll exists as a second variant for callers that don't hit the filter, after the dropping variant was used incorrectly on one such caller and silently vanished a producer. Both variants -- trim, de-dup, sort, and the length-based drop/keep split -- are used by both the CTRM contract and ticket readers and have no direct test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CtrmCustomerCodesTests.cs: an 8-char code is dropped by Normalize but kept by NormalizeKeepingAll, dedup is case-insensitive, output is sorted, null/empty collection returns empty.
findings.notes: [2026-09-28] New since the last test-gaps reconciliation (2026-09-22), part of the CTRM GraphQL work merged 2026-09-24/28. Cheap fix: pure static function, no mocking needed.
findings.resolution_notes: Added CtrmCustomerCodesTests.cs (16 cases). Pins the 7-character boundary inclusive, that Normalize drops an over-length code while NormalizeKeepingAll keeps it, that only the offending code is dropped and it is reported via the out parameter, that trimming happens BEFORE the length test in both directions, case-insensitive de-duplication keeping the first occurrence casing, case-insensitive sort ordering, null input, and blank/whitespace/null elements being discarded without appearing in dropped. Two behaviours the finding left open were resolved from the source and asserted: de-duplication and ordering are OrdinalIgnoreCase, not ordinal.

findings.title: formatAccountingMoney, the shared financial-display formatter, has zero test coverage
findings.description: The function's own doc comment says it was extracted because AccountingCurrencyPipe and the calculator report builder's reportMoneyAccounting held byte-for-byte identical formatting logic (parenthesized negatives, '$ ' prefix with a space, floored fraction digits) and had already drifted apart once. It is now the single source of truth for how every dollar figure with a sign is displayed across the app, with no test covering the negative-parentheses case, the fraction-digit floor, or null/undefined input.
findings.suggested_fix: Add accounting-money.spec.ts: positive value, negative value (parentheses, no minus sign), null/undefined input treated as 0, maxFractionDigits below 2 floored to 2, maxFractionDigits above 2 honored.
findings.notes: [2026-09-28] New since the last test-gaps reconciliation (2026-09-22). Same 'dedup that already drifted once' risk pattern as the two other new findings this run, on the money-display path this time.
findings.resolution_notes: Added accounting-money.spec.ts (9 tests) covering positive, negative rendered in parentheses with an explicit assertion that no minus sign appears, comma grouping, null and undefined treated as zero, zero and negative zero never rendering as a parenthesised zero, maxFractionDigits below 2 floored to 2, above 2 honoured, and minimum padding. Expected strings were derived by running the real implementation rather than guessed. Verified by mutation: replacing the parentheses with a minus sign failed 4 of the 9.

findings.title: CtrmKeepWarmService's cadence-gating and per-producer-set failure isolation logic has zero test coverage
findings.description: WarmActiveSetsAsync/ExecuteAsync contain several independently-gated branches read fresh every cycle so App Service config overrides apply without a restart: cadence-minutes disable-at-zero, source-must-equal-ctrm gating, keep-for-hours filtering via CtrmWarmRegistry.ActiveSets, and a per-producer-set try/catch so one set's failure doesn't end the cycle or clobber another set's warm cache. This is the same shape of untested day/interval-gating logic the now-resolved usage-aggregation-background-service-untested finding covered on the usage-aggregation service -- CtrmKeepWarmService is the CTRM-surface equivalent and was added after that finding was fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the cadence/gating decision (given now, lastRunUtc, cadenceMinutes, source config) into a pure function and unit test the zero-disables-it, source-not-ctrm-skips-it, and cadence-not-elapsed-skips-it cases directly; separately test that one producer set throwing doesn't stop the loop over the rest.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-28] New since the last test-gaps reconciliation (2026-09-22), part of the CTRM GraphQL/keep-warm work merged 2026-09-24/28.
[2026-09-28] HALF CLOSED, left open deliberately. The cadence/source gating the suggested fix asks for first is done: ShouldWarmNow(cadenceMinutes, configuredSource, nowUtc, lastRunUtc) was extracted as a pure internal static and is covered by CtrmKeepWarmServiceTests (29 cases) pinning zero and negative cadence disabling warming, the >= boundary being inclusive, a backwards clock, first run from DateTime.MinValue, Trim + OrdinalIgnoreCase source matching as equality rather than prefix or contains, each gate blocking on its own, and a 12-tick simulation showing a 5-minute cadence holds to the clock instead of drifting a minute per cycle. Verified by mutation: loosening the cadence gate, flipping the boundary to exclusive and switching the source comparison to Ordinal failed 8 of the 29. The per-producer-set failure isolation half is NOT covered and is unreachable from a unit test as the code stands: WarmActiveSetsAsync is private, its only caller sits behind a real one-minute PeriodicTimer, and CtrmContractReader and CtrmTicketReader are sealed classes with no interface that convert transport failures into non-Ok CtrmReadResults rather than exceptions, so nothing can drive the catch arm the isolation lives in. All three were verified directly rather than taken on trust. Closing that half needs an application-source change (make the method internal and put the two readers behind interfaces), which is a design decision rather than a test gap, so it was not done unilaterally. [2026-10-13] Re-verified: no change to CtrmKeepWarmService.cs's gating/isolation structure since 2026-09-28's mutation-tested pass; status and reasoning stand.
findings.resolution_notes: Both halves now covered. Gating was done on 2026-09-28 (ShouldWarmNow, 29 cases). Failure isolation needed a seam: the three CTRM reads the cycle issues now go through ICtrmWarmReads (one production adapter over the real sealed readers, registered in Program.cs), and WarmActiveSetsAsync is internal. CtrmKeepWarmCycleTests (7) pin that a set whose read throws or returns a failed status does not stop the sets after it, that a failed contract read skips that set's ticket and Spot Loads reads only, that a failed set is left alone on the next cycle while the others are warmed, that the back-off holds even if the gateway recovers inside the window, and that nothing is read with no active set. The readers themselves are unchanged; the interface is public only because the service's public constructor takes it.

findings.title: UserUsageDetailComponent's activity-partitioning and tab-derivation logic has zero test coverage, unlike its parent and sibling
findings.description: UserUsageDetailComponent (221 lines, part of the feat(usage-dashboard): manager-for-all work merged 2026-10-13) has several non-trivial computed()s with no spec: recentActivityByFeature partitions recentActivity by featureCode into a Map with an 'other' fallback bucket, currentTabRecentActivity and activeTabLabel derive from the active tab against the static tabs list, and activeDays/maxDaily/maxScreenMinutes compute chart-driving aggregates with explicit zero/empty-array edge cases (Math.max(1, ...) guards). formatAction has branching logic mapping event types to display labels. Its parent usage-dashboard.component.ts (459-line spec) and sibling manager-filter.component.ts (87-line spec) both got specs in the same feature branch; this page was left out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a component spec mirroring usage-dashboard.component.spec.ts's pattern, covering: recentActivityByFeature's 'other' fallback bucket, currentTabRecentActivity returning [] for an unmatched tab, and the maxDaily/maxScreenMinutes empty-data floor of 1.
findings.notes: [2026-10-13] New finding found by sampling the Bin Sites/Grain on Farm and Usage Dashboard Manager for All feature work merged into release_2026-10-13. Confirmed via find: no user-usage-detail.component.spec.ts exists alongside it, while both the parent dashboard and the manager-filter component it ships with do have specs.
findings.resolution_notes: Added user-usage-detail.component.spec.ts (20 tests): route params seed the signals and trigger exactly one fetch, no fetch without a userId, the error path toasts and leaves every computed signal safe, recentActivityByFeature partitioning preserves order and keeps a tab-less feature in its own bucket, the six tabs map to six distinct feature codes and swap the visible slice, activeDays counts only days with events, the chart scales floor at 1 on an all-zero window, the slice charts the last 30 of a longer window oldest-first, the default range is an inclusive 30 days ending today, the 7-day and custom ranges refetch, goBack carries the range, and the action formatters. Fixtures use the real model types with no casts. Verified by mutation: counting zero-event days as active and widening the slice to 31 failed 3 of the 20. One fallback branch (featureCode ?? other) is unreachable from the typed model and is noted rather than tested.

findings.title: Harvest pacing returns no answer for a producer whose latest delivery year is ahead of the current calendar year
findings.description: computeHarvestPacePct buckets contracts by the producer's own max delivery year (maxYear and maxYear-1) but builds its same-point-last-year cutoff from the calendar clock: new Date(today.getFullYear()-1, today.getMonth(), today.getDate()). The two only line up when maxYear equals the current calendar year. For a producer booked a year ahead, the prior-year bucket is the current calendar year while the cutoff sits a full year before it, so every dated contract in that bucket fails the cutoff, lastYearBu falls to 0, and the function returns null and the card shows nothing. Demonstrated with today = 2026-09-28: a producer with max delivery year 2026 and the same data shape returns +20%, while the identical relationship with max delivery year 2027 returns null. The failure is data-dependent in a way that hides it: the cutoff is opt-in per contract (a contract with no contractDate is always included), so the same producer returns +20% if the prior-year rows happen to carry no booking date. This function exists specifically because two earlier implementations disagreed about pacing, which is why the remaining inconsistency is worth settling deliberately.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide what the comparison should anchor to and make the cutoff follow the bucket. Anchoring to the bucket, for example new Date(maxYear-1, today.getMonth(), today.getDate()), makes the rule self-consistent for producers booked ahead, but it changes the number shown for them, so it is a product decision for whoever owns the pacing rule rather than a silent code change. The behaviour is currently pinned by a test named for it so the decision is not lost.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-28] Found while writing contract-status.spec.ts for test-gaps.contract-status-pacing-logic-untested. NOT fixed: unlike a plain defect this changes a number users read, so it needs an owner decision first. Current behaviour is documented by a passing test rather than left implicit.
[2026-10-13] Raised to high after the owner asked how this behaves across commodities. The function pools every contract regardless of commodity and uses the single latest delivery year as this-year, so a producer between crops (wheat finished and booked for next year, corn still underway) has next year's wheat compared against this year's corn-plus-wheat and reads as badly behind. That is wrong independently of the cutoff bug, which only makes the figure vanish. Both callers are the Build-a-List pacing filters (nlq-filter.service), so the effect is producers wrongly appearing in or missing from those lists. The correct shape is per-commodity pacing, each crop against its own prior year; that is a design decision, now with Marc (question drafted in Projects/Code Review/pacing-question-for-marc.md).
[2026-10-13] Closed as accepted at the owner's direction. Do not re-raise unless a change request arrives.
findings.accepted_rationale: Product owner decision 2026-10-13: leave the Build-a-List harvest-pacing filters as they are until a request to change them arrives. The two defects stay on record so the fix is ready when that happens: (1) the same-point-last-year cutoff is anchored to the calendar year, so a producer whose latest delivery year is ahead of it gets no figure; (2) the figure pools every commodity and uses the single latest delivery year, so a producer between crops reads as behind. The likely fix is per-commodity pacing anchored to each crop's own prior year. A plain-language description for the business owner is in Projects/Code Review/pacing-question-for-marc.md if the question is ever raised.

findings.title: Hover prefetch and the post-click convergence re-read ran regardless of whether the backend was reading CTRM or ODS
findings.description: Two client behaviours exist to hide CTRM GraphQL latency: a 350ms hover prefetch on the producer list, and a 4s post-click convergence re-read that swaps in anything the live read changed behind a warm trade-unit cache. Neither was gated on the data source, so neither could follow PROD between ODS and CTRM. Against ODS they buy nothing and cost up to two reads per click plus one per hovered row where PROD does one today; against CTRM the re-read is what replaces a trade-unit-cached answer that can be minutes old. Ungated, whichever way PROD is pointed one of those two costs is being paid unnecessarily.
findings.resolution_notes: Both now gate on a new environment.ctrmReadAheadEnabled flag, set per environment to match that environment's Ctrm:Source: true in local, Dev and QA, and true in Production because PROD flips to CTRM on 2026-09-29, the same day this ships. Follows the existing flag convention rather than plumbing a runtime data-source signal to the client. The tradeoff is recorded in the flag comment: being compiled in at build time, unlike Ctrm__Source it needs a client redeploy rather than a restart, so a CTRM rollback is instant while this flag would stay on until a redeploy (harmless briefly, worth a redeploy if the rollback stands). Known and accepted cost of shipping it ON: between the deploy and the moment Ctrm__Source is set to ctrm, PROD is on ODS with read-ahead active — hours of extra ODS reads, never wrong data, accepted to avoid a second client deploy on flip day.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-28] Raised in the CTRM PROD readiness pass on 2026-09-24 as an open decision and settled here ahead of the 2026-09-29 deploy.
[2026-09-28] Shipped ON in Production, corrected from an initial OFF. The first cut assumed PROD would stay on ODS after the 2026-09-29 deploy, which the committed appsettings.Production.json (Source ods, identity values empty) supports on its own — but the flip is an App Service settings change happening the same day, so OFF would have meant stale clicks and a second client deploy. Caught in review; the lesson is that a build-time flag mirroring a runtime setting has to be set from the deploy PLAN, not from what the committed config says.

findings.title: ACCEPTED-RISKS.md's 2026-09-21 banner declares IT Security countersignature closed/declined for AR-01/02/08, but AR-10 (added 2026-10-09) says those same risks are 'routed ... for IT Security countersignature' -- the two statements contradict each other in the same file
findings.description: SECURITY-REVIEWS/ACCEPTED-RISKS.md:52-65 carries a banner, decided by the project owner (CEgr) on 2026-09-21, stating in bold that 'IT Security countersignature will NOT be sought for AR-01, AR-02 or AR-08' and that the action of taking them to asksecurity@scoular.com 'is closed as declined,' calling this 'their final status, not an interim one.' AR-10 (SECURITY-REVIEWS/ACCEPTED-RISKS.md:1468-1470), added three weeks later on 2026-10-09 for the Usage Dashboard authorization-scope widening, ends with: 'Routed with AR-01/02/07/08 for IT Security countersignature, because it is an authorization-scope widening rather than a classification choice.' These are flatly inconsistent: the banner says countersignature-seeking for AR-01/02/08 is closed and declined as a final decision; AR-10 says those same three (plus AR-07, which the banner never addressed at all) are currently routed for that same countersignature. A reader of the file cannot tell whether AR-01/02/08 are awaiting IT Security sign-off or whether that question is permanently closed -- the file asserts both. This is the same self-review/traceability concern the style guide's audit-logging and least-privilege principles raise, but as a document-consistency defect rather than a re-litigation of the underlying governance decision (which this audit does not question).
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the two statements: either update the 2026-09-21 banner to note that AR-10 (and AR-07) are being routed for countersignature notwithstanding the earlier declined decision for AR-01/02/08, or correct AR-10's closing line so it does not claim AR-01/02/08 are 'routed ... for countersignature' when the banner says that was declined. Either edit is a documentation fix; no code or access-control change is implied.
findings.notes: [2026-10-13] Found while reconciling permissions findings against commits since the 2026-09-28 pass. Introduced by commit 8d91ae7a (2026-10-09), which added the AR-10 entry's closing line without updating the pre-existing 2026-09-21 countersignature banner. Not re-raising the closed access-control-risk-acceptances-lack-independent-signoff finding -- this is a narrower, new claim about internal document consistency, not about whether the underlying AR-01/02/08 decision was correct.
findings.resolution_notes: AR-10 closing line rewritten. It no longer claims AR-01/02/07/08 were routed for countersignature; it points at the 2026-09-21 banner (AR-01/02/08 closed as declined, AR-07 open) and states plainly that whether AR-10 and AR-07 go to IT Security is the project owner's call and has not been done as of 2026-10-13. No decision was invented or changed; the contradiction introduced by commit 8d91ae7a is removed.
